summary: Fix syntax corruption in executor.py and submit clean control_flow edit targeting tool failure skepticism.

edits.hypothesis: Injecting a hard-coded warning message into the conversation history immediately after a tool failure forces the LLM to explicitly disregard negative generalist VQA outputs and re-inspect the original image for subtle signs, addressing the 'uncritical_acceptance' failure mode when high-res tools fail.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt edits in toolset.py are static and may be diluted by subsequent tool observations; injecting directly into the active message stream at the point of failure ensures the instruction is immediate, contextual, and cannot be ignored by the next generation step.
edits.trigger_condition: When tool_failure_reason(obs) returns a non-None value (i.e., any tool call fails).
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000001/q000005, roi_crop failed with KeyError. The agent previously accepted 'no' from general VQA. With this edit, the agent receives a WARNING to re-examine original pixels, likely leading it to detect the subtle pathology missed by the general model. In q000002, where maira2 failed, the warning encourages skepticism of the two negative VQA models. (preservative) Success cases like q000003/q000007 do not invoke failing tools, so the warning is never injected, preserving their direct reasoning habits. (transfer) Generalizes to any task where a specialized inspection tool fails, preventing over-reliance on fallback generalists.
edits.regression_risk: Minimal. The warning is only injected on failure. It might cause slight verbosity or hesitation in edge cases where the tool failure is irrelevant to the final answer, but accuracy gain from catching false negatives outweighs this.
edits.mechanism: Injecting a hard-coded warning message into the conversation history immediately after a tool failure forces the LLM to explicitly disregard negative generalist VQA outputs and re-inspect the original image for subtle signs, addressing the 'uncritical_acceptance' failure mode when high-res tools fail.
